title: Access Control Based Solely on IP Address / Host Headers
pattern: Enforcing administrative permissions or authentication bypass boundaries by simply verifying that the incoming request's IP address matches a trusted local subnet.
why_bad: IP addresses and HTTP host headers are easily spoofed, spoofable on local networks, or hijacked via ARP poisoning, routing changes, or server side-channel vulnerabilities. Relying on network position collapses the zero-trust model.
detection: Authorization check routines that evaluate access rules using client IP variables as the primary check logic.
fix: Enforce identity-based authorization checks using cryptographic session tokens or mutual TLS (mTLS) credentials, rather than relying on network topologies.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 5, p. 78.
